references.text: Contrasting movements: Jacob's journey back to the promised land versus his sons' forced migration to Egypt.
Parallel action: Esau's flight from Canaan and Jacob's return to Canaan, illustrating two different destinies linked to brotherhood and the land.
Circular theme: Jacob's journey to his father Isaac versus his sons' journey to Jacob, marking the family's reunion across generations.
Narrative connection: The beginning (28:7) and end (31:18) of Jacob's stay in Paddan-Aram.
Theological parallel: Abraham's faith-driven journey to Canaan and Jacob's return to the same land with his entire household.
